title: Mira celebrates Diwali, the festival of light.
lines: This is Mira.
Mira is five years old and she lives in Antwerp, with Daddy, Mummy and her little brother Arjun.
Mira goes to nursery class.
But this week something very special is happening at home.
It's almost Diwali!
Diwali is the festival of light.
Mira's grandma and grandpa live far away in India, and they celebrate Diwali there too.
Mira calls them on the tablet.
Hello, Grandma!
Hello, Grandpa!
It's almost Diwali!
A few days before the festival the whole family cleans.
The whole house has to sparkle!
Daddy vacuums.
Vroommm.
Mummy washes the windows.
Mira helps with the duster.
And Arjun?
Arjun tidies up his toys.
Well, a little bit.
Hee hee.
Then they go to the shop.
Mira gets a new dress for the festival.
A pink dress with golden edges, that sparkles when she twirls.
Wow, it's so pretty!
Then at last it's Diwali.
In the morning Mira makes a rangoli with Mummy.
A rangoli is a picture on the ground in front of the door, made of coloured powder.
First Mummy draws a big flower with chalk.
Then Mira sprinkles the powder.
Pink powder for the petals.
Yellow powder for the middle.
Green powder all around, and blue dots everywhere.
Sprinkle, sprinkle.
It's a beautiful flower in every colour!
A rangoli says: welcome, everyone is welcome in our home.
In the kitchen Grandma Leela, who is visiting them, bakes lots of tasty sweets.
Round yellow laddoos, sweet balls that smell of butter and sugar.
And little squares with nuts on top.
Mira is allowed to taste a laddoo.
Mmm!
So sweet and so soft!
When it gets dark, the most beautiful moment comes.
Daddy takes a box of little oil lamps out of the cupboard.
They're made of clay, and they're called diyas.
In each lamp there's a little oil and a cotton wick.
Mummy lights the lamps, one by one, and Mira carefully puts them down.
Because fire is hot, so you have to be very careful with it!
She puts lamps on the windowsill, on the stairs, by the door and next to the rangoli.
The whole house shines with the little lights.
It's so beautiful and so warm.
Then Daddy tells a story.
The story of Prince Rama and Princess Sita.
How they came back home after a long journey, and how people put lights everywhere so they would find the way.
That's why we light lamps too, says Daddy.
To say: light is stronger than darkness, and good is stronger than bad.
Then the whole family comes to visit.
Aunts, uncles and cousins.
Everyone wears beautiful clothes.
They give each other boxes of sweets and presents.
Happy Diwali!
Happy Diwali!
everyone shouts.
They eat together, they laugh and they dance.
And then, outside in the sky: Bang!
Bang!
Fireworks!
Red, green and golden stars in the dark sky.
Ooooh!
says Arjun, and he covers his ears.
Mira holds his hand.
That night Mira falls asleep with a smile.
The next day Mira goes to school.
She has a big box with her.
What's inside?
Laddoos!
For the teacher and for all the children in the class.
Mira tells them about Diwali: about the cleaning, the rangoli, the lights and the fireworks.
And the teacher says: What a lovely festival, Mira.
Thank you for sharing it with us.
Shall we make a rangoli together too?
And that afternoon the whole class makes a big, colourful rangoli in the playground.
Happy Diwali, everyone!
